title: fix-network skill use case
description: What a coding agent does, following SKILL.md, when the developer reports a network problem on their Mac.

entities.name: Diagnose and repair the developer's network for them
entities.description: The developer reports no internet, failing DNS, a captive portal, an unreachable intranet behind a connected VPN, or broken networking after sleep; the agent diagnoses with fix-network, reports the outcomes as given and repairs only what the evidence and the developer allow.
entities.goal: Get the developer's Mac network working again, or tell them exactly what they must do themselves, without taking an unsafe or unauthorized step.
preconditions: The agent has a shell on the developer's Mac and fix-network is built or installed.
The developer has reported a network problem.
postconditions: The developer has each finding's outcome as fix-network gave it: fixed, not fixable by this tool, or reboot needed.
Without --internal-host, corporate DNS and service are reported as not verified.
A cause is reported as confirmed only with evidence.

flow.action: Tells the agent the network is broken, and names an internal host if the intranet is the problem.
Runs fix-network diagnose with --internal-host, adding -v for tunnels and split DNS or --json to parse.
Relays each finding's outcome as given: fixable with the exact fix command, not fixable by this tool, or reboot needed.
Runs fix --dry-run with the same arguments to show the plan.
Runs fix with the same arguments, adding --vpn, --fix-proxy or --allow-route-flush only with evidence from the diagnosis, and --allow-remote only if the developer accepts losing an SSH session.
Types their password into sudo in their own terminal when a privileged step needs it; the agent never asks for it in chat.
Reports the result, naming a cause as confirmed only with evidence ('it recovered' is not proof of cause), and points to the logs and original settings in the run's state directory.

alternatives.condition: A finding is not fixable by the tool or needs a reboot.
alternatives.outcome: The agent passes the advice on and does not reboot, delete network preferences, credentials or profiles, set public DNS or touch the router itself.

alternatives.condition: The VPN is Cisco Secure Client/AnyConnect.
alternatives.outcome: The tool only observes it through its routes; the developer reconnects it.

alternatives.condition: A Wi-Fi cycle leaves Wi-Fi off.
alternatives.outcome: The watchdog turns it back on; otherwise the manual rescue is networksetup -setairportpower <device> on.

relatedViews.relationship: The diagnose, fix --dry-run and fix commands the agent runs.
The same goals pursued by the developer directly.
